---
title: "Introduction to Metabolomics Data"
subtitle: "From colon-model samples to a data matrix"
---

## Training session

This 70-minute introductory session follows one central question:

> How do samples from a colon model become a metabolomics data matrix, and what must we check before interpreting it?

The materials use a small targeted HPLC dataset from an in-vitro colon-model experiment. No previous metabolomics experience is required.

## Materials

- [Open the presentation](slides/metabolomics_introduction.html)
- [Read the complete session guide](session/metabolomics_session_guide.html)
- [Download the organic-acid dataset](data/acids.csv)

## Learning outcomes

By the end of the session, participants should be able to:

1. Explain what metabolomics measures and how it complements microbiome sequencing.
2. Distinguish targeted, semi-targeted and untargeted metabolomics.
3. Recognise the main analytical platforms and their downstream data structures.
4. Describe how analytical signals become a processed data matrix.
5. Identify the metadata and quality checks needed before interpretation.

## Software

The live demonstration uses R and the `tidyverse` package. Participants can read the rendered materials without installing R.
